Activation-patching findings depend on the corruption distribution and scoring metric: changing either can change which components appear important. Natural counterfactual donors can improve interpretability, but matching observed inputs does not guarantee that hybrid internal activations remain in distribution. Denoising measures restoration under the chosen corruption; noising measures disruption under the chosen replacement. Neither establishes universal necessity or sufficiency. Test several explicitly defined corruption distributions and report continuous score changes alongside ranking metrics. Sources: [Zhang & Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042), [Heimersheim & Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.15255).

For sparse endpoint-and-length matches, the defensible methodological implication is to separate coverage from effect size. Define eligibility before measuring effects; report eligible/total recipients, donor counts, exclusions and donor reuse. Compare corruption methods on the same eligible recipients using paired differences; report broader-coverage analyses separately. Relaxing length or endpoint constraints changes the intervention, while dropping unmatched recipients changes the population represented—neither should happen silently. Matching literature emphasizes overlap and explicit target populations ([Stuart](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2943670/)). Suggested implementation controls: self-to-self patches should reproduce baseline scores within numerical tolerance; donor permutations within declared matching strata test sensitivity to donor assignment, but constitute a formal null test only with justified exchangeability. Repeat donor draws and quantify uncertainty over recipients, accounting for reused donors. Label these as proposed controls rather than established guarantees: effects remain conditional on the selected recipients, donor distribution, patch location and corruption.
